transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for reaching out. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that helps. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about the specific product you have, it's best to check with your GP or pharmacist to confirm it's okay to use.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, I'll make sure to check with my doctor. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I'd need to know how long it's been since your operation to give you a better idea. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you for the information, Dora. It's been very helpful!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.

verdict.label: pass

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside."
